contract: assert a conventionally named file installs a pending autoload at setup and runs its body only on the first reference, and that const_defined? cannot tell the two states apart while autoload? can
assert Zeitwerk::Inflector#camelize is plain underscore camelization, so http_client.rb owes HttpClient and not HTTPClient, with no special case for acronyms

assert a file that defines the acronym spelling instead raises Zeitwerk::NameError whose message is exactly the file plus the constant Zeitwerk expected, whose name is that expected constant, and which never mentions the constant the file actually defined

assert the failed autoload still leaves the wrongly named constant loaded and the file in $LOADED_FEATURES, removes the autoload, and degrades the second reference to a plain uninitialized-constant NameError

assert plain Object.autoload ends in the same state as Zeitwerk for a file that defines the wrong constant, and only keeps the constant pending when the require raises, which is the shape Zeitwerk removes the autoload for
assert an inflector override replaces the derived name outright so APIGateway autoloads, ApiGateway is never registered, and eager_load then passes
assert a file that defines no constant at all fails with the same Zeitwerk::NameError after its body has already run
assert eager_load aborts on the first mismatch in sorted order rather than reporting every mismatch, leaving the later broken file unopened, and that a second run reports the next one
assert all_expected_cpaths returns the whole path to expected constant map for the tree in one call without loading anything
assert a directory can be managed by only one loader, and that the second push_dir raises Zeitwerk::Error naming the directory before setup is ever called
assert zeitwerk 2.8.3 ships no C extension and no runtime dependency, which is why the newest release installs on an image with no compiler
case.goal: Autoload constants with Zeitwerk and work out why a correctly written class raises Zeitwerk::NameError, what the error does and does not tell you, and what eager loading really catches
